Ārya, the council agrees that ED 0 is the right fix for the reported `CSI H CSI J` regression. EL 0 should also end the row’s outgoing soft wrap when it erases the suffix. EL 2 is a sound choice for shux and agrees with VTE, kitty, and Alacritty. Two cases still produce false joins on the erase path: pending cursor wrap and a wrapped scrollback row whose visible continuation was erased.

I reviewed `974f3b2..a7ef8fa` and upstream source with three independent reviewers. The byte sequences below were traced through source. No files were modified, and no build, test, or emulator was run.

### Compatibility

The table describes the **stored outgoing row wrap**, separately from a cursor waiting to wrap on its next print.

| Sequence | xterm | kitty | Alacritty | VTE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ED 0 | Clears cursor row and rows below | Same | Same | Same |
| ED 1 | Clears rows above, preserves cursor row. Lower-right corner takes the ED 2 path | Clears rows above and clears cursor-row wrap if erase reaches the last cell | Last-cell overwrite clears cursor-row wrap. Current source skips the above-row reset when the cursor is on the second row | Clears rows above, preserves cursor row, and cuts the history-to-viewport wrap |
| ED 2 | Clears visible wraps | Same | Same. Primary can move old rows to history | Same. Primary appends a fresh screen |
| ED 3 | History only | Clears visible rows and primary history | History only | History only |
| EL 0 / 1 / 2 | Clear / preserve / preserve | Clear / clear only at last cell / clear | Same as kitty | Clear / preserve / clear |
| ECH | Clears even for an interior erase | Clears if erase reaches the last cell | Same as kitty | Preserves |
| DCH | Clears | Clears | Clears | Clears |
| IL/DL and vertical scroll | Moves surviving row flags and clears inserted rows | Same | Same | Also cuts wrap links where a restricted whole-row scroll changes adjacency |

ED and EL operate on the page or row independently of vertical scrolling margins. IL/DL honor those margins. Preserve wraps between rows that move together, and preserve the history link during ordinary full-screen upward scrolling. At a restricted scroll boundary, the VTE rule prevents unrelated rows from becoming a logical line. [xterm erase and line edits](https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/util.c#L2163-L2497) · [xterm grid operations](https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/screen.c#L1391-L1445) · [kitty erase and line edits](https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/blob/master/kitty/screen.c#L5344-L5699) · [kitty row moves](https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/blob/master/kitty/line-buf.c#L440-L488) · [Alacritty terminal operations](https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/master/alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs#L1497-L1817) · [VTE erase](https://github.com/GNOME/vte/blob/master/src/vteseq.cc#L660-L780) · [VTE scrolling and DCH](https://github.com/GNOME/vte/blob/master/src/vte.cc#L2812-L3027)

### Findings

1. **P1 — An erase can immediately recreate the wrap it just cleared.** [parser.rs:391](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs:391) · [grid.rs:1685](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1685)  
   At width 5, `ABCDE\x1b[JX` erases `E`, then puts `X` on row 2 and marks row 1 wrapped again. Both xterm and VTE retreat from pending wrap on ED 0, so `X` replaces the erased cell on row 1. Clear `auto_wrap_pending` and `after_print` together when adopting that erase behavior. Clearing only pending wrap lets a 5→4 resize recreate it from `after_print`. Give EL 0 an explicit policy too. VTE deliberately preserves pending wrap there, with the erase starting beyond the last cell. Shux currently erases that cell and still wraps. This predates the diff and affects its changed handlers. [xterm `ClearRight`](https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/blob/master/util.c#L2271-L2315) · [VTE ED 0 and EL 0](https://github.com/GNOME/vte/blob/master/src/vteseq.cc#L690-L780)

2. **P1 — `clear` can still join new output to old scrollback.** [parser.rs:1463](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs:1463) · [grid.rs:1567](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1567)  
   In a 2×5 primary grid, feed `ABCDEF\r\n\x1b[H\x1b[JXYZ`, then widen to 10. `ABCDE` has already scrolled into history with its outgoing wrap set. Reflow joins it to `XYZ` and brings `ABCDEXYZ` into the viewport. When ED replaces the first visible row in full, terminate the last history row’s outgoing wrap while retaining its cells. Preserve that link when the first visible row keeps a prefix of the original continuation. This is another case of the same false join, present on both revisions.

3. **P1 — DCH leaves a false continuation.** [grid.rs:1879](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1879)  
   At width 5, `ABCDEFG\x1b[1;2H\x1b[P` followed by a widen joins `FG` to the edited `ACDE` row. All four comparators clear the outgoing wrap on an effective DCH. Clear it when the delete shifts cells and fills the right edge. This predates the diff.

4. **P1 — Restricted line edits can join unrelated rows.** [grid.rs:1368](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1368) · [parser.rs:1511](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs:1511)  
   In a 4×5 grid, `\x1b[2;3r\x1b[4;1HZ\x1b[2;1HABCDEF\x1b[2;1H\x1b[L` moves wrapped `ABCDE` to row 3, discards `F`, and leaves `Z` on row 4. Widening joins `ABCDEZ`. A DL example is `ABCDEF\x1b[3;1HZ\x1b[2;1H\x1b[M`, which deletes `F` and moves `Z` under wrapped `ABCDE`. Cut the outgoing links at the splice boundaries where adjacency changes. Keep internal links between surviving rows. This predates the diff.

5. **P1 — ED 3 discards the visible page under the xterm interpretation.** [parser.rs:1480](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs:1480)  
   `VISIBLE\x1b[3J` removes `VISIBLE` in shux and kitty. xterm, Alacritty, and VTE keep it. For xterm compatibility, call only `clear_scrollback()` and assert that visible text survives. This is an existing behavior with a test, so it warrants a separate compatibility decision.

6. **P2 — The tests leave the partial-erase boundary and exact colors unproved.** [lib.rs:2163](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs:2163) · [lib.rs:2208](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs:2208)  
   The smoke test exercises the original failure mechanism across several widths and checks that the sentinel stays on its own row. It constructs a Bash-style stream, and the 60-space variant still echoes `%40s`. Its color assertion would accept one correct leading cell followed by the wrong non-default colors. Assert the contiguous per-cell background run. The flag test homes before ED 0 and EL 0, so both erase the entire cursor row. Add `ABCDEFG\x1b[1;3H\x1b[K` at width 5 and verify that `AB` and `FG` stay separate after widening. Add an interior ECH preservation case. For ECH that reaches the physical right edge, `ABCDEFG\x1b[1;3H\x1b[3X` gives the same false join on widen today. I would clear the flag in that edge case and keep interior ECH VTE-compatible.

### What the flag affects

- Copy mode and ordinary text capture already emit physical-row newlines. Shell-input reconstruction and primary-screen reflow use `Row::wrapped` to join rows. Those are the paths where stale flags change the result. [copy_mode.rs:785](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs:785) · [lib.rs:631](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs:631) · [lib.rs:1489](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs:1489)
- The suffix erase resets cell metadata and expands over intersecting wide pairs. It consumes the trailing wide-glyph gap mark as part of the erased suffix. Reflow only interprets trailing gap marks on wrapped rows. The alternate screen resizes as a canvas, and the helper acts on the active grid. The history seam is the exception that requires an explicit boundary update. [grid.rs:449](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:449) · [grid.rs:1709](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs:1709) · [lib.rs:1347](/private/tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs:1347)

I would keep the three outgoing-wrap changes and fix the pending-wrap and history cases in #301. The DCH, restricted-scroll, and ED 3 findings can be reviewed independently.

FIX

### 1. Is this the right rule?

The core rule in `a7ef8fa` — clearing the cursor row's soft wrap on **ED 0**, **EL 0**, and **EL 2** while leaving mid-row **EL 1** and mid-row **ECH** alone — is right for the common case, and matches xterm/VTE for those five sequences. However, it is **incomplete** as a terminal-wide soft-wrap invariant because it only guards the cursor row on `ED 0`/`EL 0`/`EL 2`, leaving several other erase and scroll boundaries able to glue unrelated rows together on reflow.

#### Cross-terminal comparison (soft-wrap flag clearing)

| Sequence | xterm (`LINEWRAPPED` on row) | VTE (`soft_wrapped` on row) | Alacritty (`WRAPLINE` on last cell) | kitty (`continued` on *next* row) | `shux-vt` @ `a7ef8fa` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ED 0** (`CSI 0 J`) | Clears cur row + rows below | Clears cur row + rows below | Clears cur row + rows below | Clears cur row's outgoing wrap + rows below (and incoming wrap if `col == 0`) | Clears cur row + rows below; **misses `raw[sb-1]` when `(0,0)`** |
| **ED 1** (`CSI 1 J`) | Clears rows above; leaves cur row | Clears rows above; leaves cur row | Clears rows above; clears cur row **iff `col == cols-1`** | Clears incoming wraps `0..=cur_y`; leaves cur row's outgoing wrap | Clears rows above; **misses `raw[sb-1]` and cur row at `col == cols-1`** |
| **ED 2** (`CSI 2 J`) | Clears all visible rows | Scrolls/clears visible (no wrap to history) | Clears all visible rows | Clears all visible rows + incoming wrap on row 0 | Clears all visible rows; **misses `raw[sb-1]`** |
| **ED 3** (`CSI 3 J`) | Scrollback only (visible untouched) | Scrollback only | Scrollback only | Scrollback only (+ breaks row 0's wrap from history) | Clears visible + scrollback *(pre-existing divergence, [lib.rs:4766](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L4766))* |
| **EL 0** (`CSI 0 K`) | Clears cur row (`ClearRight`) | Clears cur row | Clears cur row | Clears cur row's outgoing wrap | Clears cur row |
| **EL 1** (`CSI 1 K`) | Leaves cur row | Leaves cur row | Clears cur row **iff `col == cols-1`** | Clears cur row's *incoming* wrap (`cur_y - 1`), leaves outgoing | Leaves cur row (**even at `col == cols-1`**) |
| **EL 2** (`CSI 2 K`) | Clears cur row (`ClearLine`) | Clears cur row | Clears cur row | Clears cur row's incoming & outgoing wraps | Clears cur row |
| **ECH** (`CSI Ps X`) | Leaves cur row | Leaves cur row | Clears cur row **iff `col + n >= cols`** | Leaves cur row's outgoing wrap | Leaves cur row (**even if `col + n >= cols`**) |
| **DCH** (`CSI Ps P`) | Clears cur row (`DeleteChar`) | Clears cur row | Clears cur row | Leaves outgoing wrap | Leaves cur row *(intentionally pinned for wide-gap tests, [lib.rs:1975-2028](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L1975-L2028))* |
| **IL / DL / SU / SD / RI / scroll regions** | Blanks new rows; no reflow | Clears new rows + region boundaries | Blanks new rows | Clears new rows + region boundaries | Blanks new rows; **leaves stale `wrapped` at `sb+top-1` and `sb+bottom`** |

**Should also end a soft wrap:**
- **Whole/top-of-screen clears across scrollback (`raw[sb - 1]`)**: `ED 0` at `(0, 0)`, `ED 1`, `ED 2`, and `DECALN` (`ESC # 8`) — visible row 0 was wiped clean and no longer continues scrollback row `sb - 1`.
- **Scroll-region / line-edit boundaries**: `scroll_down_n` (`IL`, `SD`, `RI`) must clear `raw[sb + bottom].wrapped` (its continuation was discarded) and `raw[sb + top - 1].wrapped` (if `sb + top > 0`, since `top` is now a fresh blank row). Partial-region `scroll_up_n` (`DL`, `SU`, `LF` inside a partial region) must clear `raw[sb + top - 1].wrapped` (if `sb + top > 0`, since old `top` was discarded rather than scrolled into scrollback).
- **`EL 1` / `ED 1` when `cursor.col == cols - 1`** (and `ECH` when `col + n >= cols` if following Alacritty's "any erase reaching the right margin" rule, though xterm/VTE leave `ECH` alone): erasing columns `0..cols` leaves a completely blank row that no longer runs into the next row.
- **`DCH` (design trade-off)**: xterm, VTE, and Alacritty all clear soft wrap on `DCH`. `shux-vt` currently preserves it with explicit wide-gap fill logic ([grid.rs:1890-1901](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1890-L1901)) and three unit tests ([lib.rs:1975-2028](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L1975-L2028)). If `DCH` stays preserving wrap, note that full-row `DCH` (`\x1b[1;1H\x1b[5P`) still reproduces #301.

**Should NOT end a soft wrap:**
- **Full-screen `scroll_up_n(0, rows - 1, n)`**: visible row 0 moves into scrollback right after `raw[sb - 1]`, so `raw[sb - 1].wrapped` must survive.
- **Mid-row `EL 1` (`col < cols - 1`)** and **mid-row `ECH` (`col + n < cols`)**: the right end of the row is intact.
- **`EL 0` / `EL 2` on `cursor.row` must NOT clear `row[cursor.row - 1].wrapped`** (within the viewport): line editors like readline/bash emit `\b\x1b[K` at `(row, 0)` when backspacing the first character of a continuation row; keeping `row - 1` wrapped preserves the logical command line when the user retypes.
- **`DECSTBM` (`CSI Pt;Pb r`)**: changes margins and homes cursor without touching row content.
- **`ICH` (`CSI @`)** (when already preserving per [lib.rs:1898-1901](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L1898-L1901), [lib.rs:2111-2116](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L2111-L2116)).

---

### 2. Does clearing the flag break anything that relies on it?

No regressions from clearing `row.wrapped` in `erase_to_row_end`:

- **Copy & capture**: `capture_text` ([lib.rs:1489-1521](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L1489-L1521)), `glance_text` ([grid.rs:1132-1147](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1132-L1147)), and copy mode `extract_from` ([copy_mode.rs:723-795](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-ui/src/copy_mode.rs#L723-L795)) do not read `row.wrapped`. `input_rows` ([lib.rs:631-664](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L631-L664)) does read `row.wrapped` and strictly benefits: an erased prompt row is no longer concatenated with the row below it, while backspacing on a continuation row (`EL 0` on row 1) still leaves row 0 wrapped.
- **Reflow on later resize**: `resize_reflowing_columns` ([grid.rs:1567-1591](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1567-L1591)) now ends the `LogicalLine` at the erased row instead of absorbing the next row as padding or text.
- **Wide-glyph gap mark (`Cell::meta`)**: Safe. `erase_to_row_end` erases `from..cols` via `Cell::reset` ([cell.rs:328](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/cell.rs#L328)), which clears `CellMeta::WIDE_GAP` on the erased tail including `cols - 1`; `Row::reflow_cells` ([grid.rs:1709-1720](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1709-L1720)) only strips trailing gaps when `self.wrapped == true`, and `clear_stale_gaps` ([grid.rs:1910-1916](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1910-L1916)) sanitizes any non-trailing gap before `ICH`/`DCH`.
- **Alternate screen & synchronized output**: Safe. `Row::wrapped` lives directly on `Row` (outside `Arc<Vec<Cell>>`), `Presented<Grid>` freezes before `erase_chars`, `resize_canvas` ignores `wrapped`, and `is_blank_canvas`/`is_actually_blank` stay consistent.
- **Scrollback**: Clearing `cursor.row.wrapped` doesn't harm scrollback, **but** scrollback exposes Finding 1 below: `raw[sb - 1].wrapped` is *not* cleared when `clear` wipes visible row 0.
- **Cursor `after_print` and `auto_wrap_pending`**: Unchanged and unbroken. `ED`/`EL` never touched either flag before; on a wrapped row, repositioning the cursor back onto row 0 already cleared `after_print` and `auto_wrap_pending`, and on an unwrapped row `wrapped` was already `false`.
- **Dirty tracking (minor regression)**: Calling `visible_row_mut_marked` after `erase_chars` widens the dirty range from `from..cols` to `0..cols` and bumps `mutations` twice (Finding 5).

---

### 3. Do the tests prove the claim?

- **`a_clear_does_not_join_the_next_line_onto_a_wrapped_row`** ([lib.rs:2176-2205](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L2176-L2205)) genuinely proves the exact #301 regression: the echoed command in `smoke_301` is 144 bytes (soft-wrapping row 0 at 80 cols), followed by `\x1b[H\x1b[J` and three coloured fills; without the fix, shrinking drops the brown row and shifts green/`DONE-mark` up, failing both assertions. However, it starts with empty scrollback (missing Finding 1) and `row_bgs` only checks `row[0].style.bg` + non-default cell count rather than verifying every cell's colour in `0..kept` and `kept..cols`.
- **`erasing_to_the_end_of_a_row_ends_its_soft_wrap`** ([lib.rs:2208-2219](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs#L2208-L2219)) proves the flag change only partially: it tests `ED 0`, `EL 0`, and `EL 2` **only from `(0, 0)`** (`\x1b[H`), never from mid-row (`from > 0`), never tests `ECH` (despite the commit message's explicit claim about `ECH`), never tests `ED 1`, and never tests `EL 1` at the last column (`cols - 1`).

---

### Findings

1. **[P1] `clear` / `ED 0` / `ED 1` / `ED 2` / `DECALN` leave `raw[sb - 1].wrapped == true` across the scrollback boundary**
   - **Location:** [parser.rs:1461-1479](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L1461-L1479), [grid.rs:1404-1411](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1404-L1411), [grid.rs:1423-1430](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1423-L1430), [grid.rs:1444-1452](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1444-L1452)
   - **Failing byte sequence:** On a `4x5` terminal, `b"1\r\n2\r\n3\r\nABCDEF\r\n\r\n\r\n\x1b[H\x1b[JHELLO"` (or `\x1b[2J\x1b[HHELLO`), then `resize(4, 10)` -> visible row 0 becomes `"ABCDEHELLO"` (the pre-`clear` scrollback row is fused with post-`clear` output and pulled back into the viewport). Same with the #301 workload on `24x80` when a wrapped line's head is at `raw[sb - 1]`: after `clear` + 40 blue spaces + `\r\n` + 40 brown spaces, `resize(10, 40)` drops all 40 blue spaces and pulls 40 chars of scrollback onto visible row 0.
   - **Fix:** Clear `self.raw[sb - 1].wrapped = false` when `sb > 0` in `clear_visible`, `clear_above`, `fill_alignment_pattern`, and in `ED 0` when `cursor.row == 0 && cursor.col == 0` (and `ED 1` when `cursor.row == 0`).

2. **[P1] `scroll_down_n` (`IL`/`SD`/`RI`) and partial-region `scroll_up_n` (`DL`/`SU`/region-`LF`) leave stale `wrapped = true` at region boundaries**
   - **Location:** [grid.rs:1351-1360](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1351-L1360), [grid.rs:1368-1387](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1368-L1387)
   - **Failing byte sequences** (all on `4x5`, followed by `resize(4, 10)`):
     - `SD` (full screen, no custom scroll region): `b"1\r\n2\r\nABCDEFG\x1b[1T\x1b[4;1H\r\nNEXT"` -> row 2 becomes `"ABCDENEXT"` (`raw[3]` kept `wrapped = true` after `"FG"` was discarded, then scrolled up and glued to `"NEXT"`).
     - `SD` with scroll region above status bar: `b"\x1b[2;1HABCDEFG\x1b[4;1HSTAT!\x1b[1;3r\x1b[1T"` -> row 2 becomes `"ABCDESTAT!"`.
     - `IL` (full screen): `b"ABCDEFG\x1b[2;1H\x1b[1LHI"` -> row 0 becomes `"ABCDEHI"`.
     - `DL` (full screen): `b"ABCDEFG\r\nNEXT\x1b[2;1H\x1b[1M"` -> row 0 becomes `"ABCDENEXT"`.
   - **Fix:** In `scroll_down_n`, clear `self.raw[sb + bottom].wrapped = false` and, if `sb + top > 0`, `self.raw[sb + top - 1].wrapped = false`. In the partial-region `else` branch of `scroll_up_n`, clear `self.raw[sb + top - 1].wrapped = false` if `sb + top > 0` (leaving full-screen `scroll_up_n` intact so wrapped lines scroll into scrollback).

3. **[P1] `EL 1` and `ED 1` at the last column (`col == cols - 1`) erase the entire row without clearing `wrapped`**
   - **Location:** [parser.rs:1468-1475](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L1468-L1475), [parser.rs:1493-1495](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L1493-L1495) (and [parser.rs:1541-1545](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L1541-L1545) for `ECH` when `col + n >= cols`)
   - **Failing byte sequence:** On a `4x5` terminal, `b"ABCDEFG\x1b[1;5H\x1b[1K\x1b[H\x1b[44m   \x1b[0m\r\n\x1b[42m   \x1b[0m"` (or `\x1b[1;5H\x1b[1J`), then `resize(4, 3)` -> the green row vanishes. Likewise `b"ABCDEFG\x1b[1;5H\x1b[1K"` then `resize(4, 10)` -> row 0 becomes `"     FG"`. (Same for `b"ABCDEFG\x1b[1;1H\x1b[5X\x1b[44m   \x1b[0m\r\n\x1b[42m   \x1b[0m"` if `ECH` reaching the right margin should also end wrap.)
   - **Fix:** Clear `wrapped = false` on `cursor.row` in `EL 1` and `ED 1` when `self.cursor.col + 1 >= cols` (and decide explicitly whether `ECH` when `self.cursor.col.saturating_add(n) >= cols` should match Alacritty or xterm/VTE).

4. **[P1] `wrap_to_next_line` sets `wrapped = true` when the cursor sits below the scroll region on the last row and cannot advance**
   - **Location:** [parser.rs:581-599](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L581-L599)
   - **Failing byte sequence:** On a `4x5` terminal, `b"\x1b[1;2r\x1b[4;1HABCDEF\x1b[r\x1b[4;1H\r\nNEXT"`, then `resize(4, 10)` -> row 2 becomes `"FBCDENEXT"` instead of `"FBCDE"` and `"NEXT"`.
   - **Fix:** Move `self.grid.visible_row_mut_marked(self.cursor.row).wrapped = true;` inside the `if self.cursor.row == self.scroll_region.bottom` and `else if self.cursor.row + 1 < self.grid.rows()` branches, so it is never set when the cursor stays on the same row.

5. **[P2] `erase_to_row_end` defeats partial-row dirty tracking and double-bumps `mutations`**
   - **Location:** [parser.rs:391-396](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L391-L396)
   - **Failing byte sequence:** On a `2x8` terminal, `vt.process(b"ABCDEF"); vt.take_dirty_regions(); vt.process(b"\x1b[1;5H\x1b[K");` -> `vt.take_dirty_regions()` reports `0..8` instead of `4..8`, even though `0..4` was untouched and `wrapped` was already `false`.
   - **Fix:** Move `erase_to_row_end` into `Grid` alongside `erase_chars`, clearing `r.wrapped = false` in the same call with a single `bump_mutations()` and `dirty.mark_range(row, range, ...)`.

6. **[P2] `DCH` full-row delete leaves `wrapped = true` (tension with existing wide-gap tests)**

reviews.content:
Overall, codex’s review is **well-grounded in both upstream and local source** and makes several high-value catches, but it **misses a real regression introduced by the diff itself**, **recommends a DCH change that breaks three existing `shux` tests and dedicated `wide_gap` code**, leaves **parallel gaps in its own Findings 1, 2, 4, and 6**, and **inflates pre-existing/out-of-scope compatibility choices to P1**.

*(All `shux` line numbers below are verified against commit `a7ef8fa`, the exact revision in `974f3b2..a7ef8fa` that codex reviewed.)*

---

### Strengths

- **Accurate local & upstream citations.** All 16 local `file:line` references (at `a7ef8fa`) and all 7 upstream GitHub line ranges (`xterm`, `kitty`, `Alacritty`, `VTE`) point to the exact functions described.
- **High-accuracy upstream compatibility table.** Almost every cell checks out against upstream source—including subtle quirks like Alacritty’s real off-by-one bug in `ED 1` (`if cursor.line > 1` skipping row 0 when on the second row, `alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs:1761`), xterm’s `ED 1` lower-right corner delegating to `ED 2` (`util.c:2460-2464`), xterm’s `EL 2` preserving wrap (`util.c:2346-2353`), VTE’s `ED 1` cutting the history-to-viewport wrap (`vteseq.cc:208-210`), and kitty’s `ED 3` clearing visible rows + primary history (`screen.c:5482-5528`).
- **Sharp catch on `after_print` interaction (Finding 1).** Tracing `ABCDE\x1b[J` followed by a 5→4 resize through [`position_for_offset`](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/grid.rs#L1685) (`after_print && (target == self.cols || self.end_col >= self.cols)`) is genuinely non-obvious and right: clearing only `auto_wrap_pending` without clearing `after_print` really does re-synthesize pending wrap on shrink. Also accurately diagnoses that shux’s `EL 0` under pending wrap currently takes the worst of both worlds (erases the last cell *and* still wraps).
- **Verified reproducers for scrollback seam & IL/DL (Findings 2 & 4).** Both `ABCDEF\r\n\x1b[H\x1b[JXYZ` (2×5 → widen to 10 pulling `ABCDEXYZ` into the viewport) and the two IL/DL splice reproducers trace cleanly to real false joins in `a7ef8fa`.
- **On-target test critique (Finding 6).** Every defect flagged in the new tests is real: `smoke_301(60)` echoes `%40s`, `row_bgs` only checks `row[0].style.bg` plus a count of *any* non-default cells (so mixed/non-contiguous wrong colors pass), `erasing_to_the_end_of_a_row_ends_its_soft_wrap` homes before `ED 0`/`EL 0` (leaving mid-row suffix erase and widen-reflow untested), and `ECH` is named in the commit message with no test.

---

### Errors & Concrete Misses

1. **Missed a direct regression introduced by `a7ef8fa` itself (dirty tracking & mutation double-bump).**  
   In [`parser.rs`](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/parser.rs#L391-L396) at `a7ef8fa`, the new helper `erase_to_row_end` does:
   ```rust
   self.grid.erase_chars(self.cursor.row, from, cols.saturating_sub(from), bg);
   self.grid.visible_row_mut_marked(self.cursor.row).wrapped = false;
   ```
   `erase_chars` already bumps `grid.mutations` once and marks only the erased column slice `from..cols` (expanded for split wide pairs) dirty. Calling `visible_row_mut_marked` (`grid.rs:1178-1182`) right afterward **dirties the entire row `0..cols`** (breaking partial-row dirty tracking for mid-row `EL 0`/`ED 0`) and **double-bumps `grid.mutations`**. Codex specifically cited `parser.rs:391` and missed this regression in the diff it was reviewing.

2. **Finding 3 (DCH) contradicts three existing `shux` unit tests and dedicated `wide_gap` logic without noticing.**  
   Codex recommends clearing `Row::wrapped` in `Grid::delete_chars` (`grid.rs:1879`) as a P1, without mentioning that `shux` explicitly relies on `DCH` preserving `Row::wrapped`:
   - Three existing unit tests in [`lib.rs`](file:///tmp/c301/wt/crates/shux-vt/src/lib.rs) (`deleting_the_wide_gap_leaves_a_gap` at `L1975`, `a_blank_shifted_into_the_last_column_is_not_a_gap` at `L1983`, and `deleting_before_a_wide_gap_adds_no_space` at `L2023` in `a7ef8fa`) execute `\x1b[1P` on row 0 and assert the row still joins with row 1 on resize.
   - `Grid::delete_chars` (`grid.rs:1887-1894`) has dedicated `Cell::wide_gap` fill propagation that is *only* ever read by `Row::reflow_cells()` when `self.wrapped == true` (`grid.rs:1710`).  
   Applying Finding 3 as written immediately breaks all three tests and turns that `wide_gap` logic into dead code. By contrast, in Finding 5 codex explicitly flagged an existing test as requiring a compatibility decision—here it missed both the tests and the intentional implementation right inside the function it cited.

3. **Finding 5 mischaracterizes the existing `ED 3` test and misses a `mutations` side effect.**  
   Codex notes *"This is an existing behavior with a test"*, referring to `test_ed_clear_screen_and_scrollback` (`lib.rs:4759`). That test only feeds five `\n`s (never writes visible text) before `\x1b[3J`, so `assert_eq!(vt.grid().visible_row(0)[0].ch, ' ')` passes regardless of whether `ED 3` clears the visible viewport. Meanwhile, `clear_scrollback()` deliberately does **not** advance `grid.mutations()` (`grid.rs:956`), so removing `clear_visible(bg)` from `ED 3` changes whether `\x1b[3J` bumps `content_revision`/dirty state—something codex didn’t mention.

4. **Minor factual inaccuracies in the compatibility table and Finding 1’s headline:**
   - **VTE `IL/DL and vertical scroll`:** Codex says VTE cuts wrap links *"where a restricted whole-row scroll changes adjacency."* In fact, VTE’s `scroll_text_down` (`src/vte.cc:2946-2947`) unconditionally calls `set_hard_wrapped(top - 1)` even on an **unrestricted** full-screen downward scroll (`SD`/`RI`/`IL` at row 0), cutting the history-to-viewport link.
   - **Finding 1 headline vs. reproducer:** The title says *"An erase can immediately recreate the wrap it just cleared,"* but in `ABCDE\x1b[JX` row 1’s stored `wrapped` flag was still `false` before `\x1b[J` (only `auto_wrap_pending` was set). Reproducing a *recreated* cleared wrap requires an already-wrapped row (e.g., `ABCDEF\x1b[HABCDE\x1b[JX`).

---

### Weaknesses & Blind Spots

- **Finding 1 (pending wrap) stops at `ED 0` and `EL 0`, missing `EL 2` (in this diff) and every other erase/edit op.**  
  In `shux`, *none* of `ED 1`, `ED 2`, `EL 1`, `EL 2`, `ECH`, `DCH`, `ICH`, `IL`, `DL`, `SU`, or `SD` clear `auto_wrap_pending` (and `IL`/`DL`/`SU`/`SD` at `parser.rs:1361` clear `after_print` while leaving `auto_wrap_pending` set). Most directly for this diff, `EL 2` now routes through `erase_to_row_end(0, bg)`: at width 5, `ABCDE\x1b[2KX` erases the entire row, clears `wrapped`, leaves `auto_wrap_pending = true`, and then `X` marks the blank row wrapped and writes on row 2. Both xterm (`ResetWrap` in `ClearInLine2`/`ClearScreen`) and VTE (`maybe_retreat_cursor` in `clear_current_line`/`clear_screen`/`clear_to_bol`/`erase_characters`) clear pending wrap across those handlers, not just `ED 0`.

- **Finding 2 (history seam) scopes the fix too narrowly to `"When ED replaces the first visible row in full"`.**  
  The exact same `ABCDEXYZ` false join on widen happens without `ED` at all:
  - **`EL 0` at `(0, 0)` and `EL 2` on row 0** (both modified in this diff): `ABCDEF\r\n\x1b[H\x1b[KXYZ` and `ABCDEF\r\n\x1b[H\x1b[2KXYZ`.
  - **`ED 1` / `EL 1` on row 0** (`\x1b[1;1H\x1b[1J` or `\x1b[1;3H\x1b[1K`): erases cell 0 of the continuation (no prefix of the original continuation survives), yet doesn’t replace the row "in full"; VTE unconditionally cuts `insert_delta - 1` on every `ED 1` (`vteseq.cc:208-210`).
  - **`DECALN` (`ESC # 8`)** (`grid.rs:1423`): replaces visible row 0 with `'E'`s without breaking `raw[sb - 1].wrapped`.
  - **Full-screen `SD` / `RI` / `IL` at row 0** (`grid.rs:1368`): inserts a blank visible row 0 directly beneath a wrapped scrollback row.

- **Finding 4 (IL/DL splice boundaries) misses the `wrap_to_next_line` ordering trap.**  
  In `shux` (`parser.rs:585-588`), `wrap_to_next_line` sets `row.wrapped = true` **before** calling `self.grid.scroll_up(top, bottom)`. Implementing codex’s advice (*"Cut the outgoing links at the splice boundaries where adjacency changes"*) naively inside `scroll_up_n` would clear the wrap flag on the bottom row that *just* wrapped onto the newly scrolled-in line, breaking normal soft-wrapping at the bottom margin. Also, Finding 4 cites `parser.rs:1511` instead of `grid.rs:1351` (`scroll_up_n`), and its second example (`ABCDEF\x1b[3;1HZ\x1b[2;1H\x1b[M`) happens on an *unrestricted* screen (not restricted margins), while `SU`/`SD`/`RI`/`IND` share the same paths.

- **Finding 6 applies an inconsistent right-edge rule to `ECH` vs. `EL 1` / `ED 1`.**  
  Codex flags `ABCDEFG\x1b[1;3H\x1b[3X` (ECH reaching the physical right edge) as causing a false join on widen and recommends clearing `wrapped` there (which is kitty/Alacritty’s rule, though codex describes interior preservation as "VTE-compatible"). Yet it ignores the symmetric case where `EL 1` or `ED 1` reaches the right edge (`ABCDEFG\x1b[1;5H\x1b[1K` or `\x1b[1;5H\x1b[1J`), which erases all 5 cells of row 0 while leaving `wrapped = true` and joins 5 blank cells onto `FG` on widen—the exact reason kitty and Alacritty clear `wrapped` on `EL 1`/`ED 1` at the last column too.

- **Severity inflation and unfocused `FIX` verdict.**  
  Five of six findings are rated **P1**, bundling pre-existing behavior untouched by `974f3b2..a7ef8fa` (Findings 3, 4, 5)—including one that matches kitty and that codex itself calls a separate compatibility decision, and one that breaks three existing tests—at the same priority level as erase-path regressions directly affecting #301. Static-only tracing (no `cargo test`) is also what let Finding 3’s test conflict slip through.

synthesis.content:
Ārya, **FIX before merging #301.** Keep the change that clears the cursor row’s outgoing soft wrap on ED 0, EL 0, and EL 2. ED 0 is the right fix for the reported `CSI H CSI J` regression. The patch also needs to handle pending cursor wrap, break stale links from scrollback, and preserve partial-row dirty tracking.

### Required for #301

| Finding | Change and regression check |
|---|---|
| **Pending wrap survives erase** | At width 5, `ABCDE\x1b[JX` puts `X` on row 2 after erasing `E`. ED 0 should clear both `auto_wrap_pending` and `after_print` so the next print stays on row 1. Clearing only the first flag allows a 5→4 resize to restore pending wrap. Cover EL 2 as well with `ABCDE\x1b[2KX`. For EL 0, explicitly choose whether to cancel pending wrap and erase the last cell, or follow VTE and preserve pending wrap with the erase starting beyond the last cell. Shux currently erases the last cell and still wraps. |
| **A clear can join new output to old scrollback** | In a 2×5 grid, `ABCDEF\r\n\x1b[H\x1b[JXYZ` followed by widening to 10 can produce `ABCDEXYZ`. Cover ED 0, EL 0, and EL 2 when they fully erase the first visible row. Clear the last history row’s outgoing wrap while retaining its cells. Preserve the history link on a suffix erase that leaves the original continuation’s prefix intact. Also preserve the incoming link between visible rows for the readline backspace-and-retype case. |
| **The patch dirties the entire row and counts the mutation twice** | `erase_chars` already marks the affected range and increments the mutation counter. `visible_row_mut_marked` repeats the count and marks the whole row. Update the wrap flag within the same grid operation. For a plain mid-row erase at column 5 on an 8-column grid, assert the dirty range stays `4..8` and the mutation count advances once. |

The existing smoke test exercises the original failure mechanism across several widths. Tighten it to check the exact background color of each cell in the expected run and the default background after it. Make the echoed `%Ns` match the fill width. Add a mid-row suffix erase followed by widening. At width 5, `ABCDEFG\x1b[1;3H\x1b[K` should leave `AB` and `FG` on separate logical lines. Add an interior ECH case to pin wrap preservation.

### Follow-up work

- **Scroll and line-edit boundaries.** IL, DL, and scrolling can leave wrap links pointing at unrelated rows after adjacency changes. Preserve links between rows that move together and across ordinary full-screen upward scrolling into history. Bottom-margin autowrap also needs to retain the new link into the inserted row. Separately, `wrap_to_next_line` should set the flag only when the cursor actually advances or scrolls.
- **Other erase boundaries.** ED 1, ED 2, prefix erases on the first visible row, and DECALN can also leave a stale history link. Decide the right-edge policy for ED 1, EL 1, and ECH together. Terminals differ on these cases.
- **DCH and ED 3 compatibility.** DCH can produce false joins, but shux deliberately preserves its wrap for wide-glyph gaps, with three tests depending on it. Change that behavior alongside an explicit decision about gap handling. ED 3 is a separate compatibility choice. Shux and kitty clear the visible page, while xterm, VTE, and Alacritty preserve it. The existing shux test starts with a blank viewport, so it cannot distinguish those behaviors. Any change should test visible text and account for content revision tracking.

The review evidence is source tracing at `a7ef8fa`. The byte sequences above still need runtime verification before merge.
